newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty flat vs basket ahead of U.S. payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty flat vs basket ahead of U.S. payrolls.

text.p: The Polish zloty held virtually unchanged against the basket of currencies in thin early trade and dealers said there were nearly no client-orders to drive trade on Friday.
"Trade is likely to remain light as there are not many market-moving client orders today to stir up turnover," said Malgorzata Sawicka of Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said banks fine-tuned positions ahead of U.S. payroll data due at 1230 GMT, which could shake up major rates but will be released after the Polish market closes.
At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 1.72/1.63 percent from the trading band centre, nearly flat from 1.72/1.66 percent at 0700 GMT and Thursday's close at 1.70/1.65 percent from parity.
It was at 2.7505/25 to the dollar, flat from 2.7510/20 at opening and down from 2.7480/90 on Thursday. It was at 1.8525/45 to the mark, down from opening's 1.8518/28 and up from Thursday's 1.8538/49.
One-day deposits held above the main 14-day reverse repo rate of 19.05 percent as the market remained short-of-cash.
Overnight rates were at 19.25/19.55, slightly higher than 19.15/19.45 percent at 0640 GMT and Thursday's 19.2/19.5.
Tomorrow/next rates were flat from opening and Thursday's close at 19.20/19.55 percent.
The National Bank of Poland refrained from offering a reverse repo or NPB-bill sale on Friday, the third day running it had not staged a drainage operation.
On the secondary market benchmark 52-week T-bills bought at Monday's auction were quoted at 19.40/19.35 percent against an average yield of 19.39 percent at the tender.
